cot:
The piano is sounding overly squashed with the compressor wet mix sitting at 50%, pushing a 2:1 ratio that dulls the natural hammer transients and flattens the dynamic life. To restore the instrument’s articulation, I’ll dial the compression ratio down to nearly transparent at 1.01:1 and pull the wet blend down to 17% so it only gently caps the loudest peaks. The threshold needs to drop slightly to -16.52 dB to reduce overall engagement, and I’ll cut the makeup gain from +2.0 dB to -0.47 dB to keep the noise floor quiet and preserve the original level. The attack should be tightened to capture transients instantly, while the release is slowed for a smoother, less pumping decay. The expander threshold drops to -52.51 dB with a steep ratio to quietly manage the tail without affecting the main body. Commit: dial the wet mix down to 17% (drywet_fraction 0.17), set comp_ratio to 1.01 (cmp_ratio -8.106), drop comp_threshold_db to -16.52 (cmp_th -16.518), pull exp_threshold_db to -52.51 (exp_th -52.507), steepen exp_ratio to 19.94 (exp_ratio 5.678), cut makeup_db to -0.47 (make_up -0.466), tighten attack_coef_sigmoid to 0.0 (at -10.48), and slow release_coef_sigmoid to 0.049 (rt -2.966).

The noise gate is currently completely off, allowing room resonance and string bleed to linger and muddy the low-mid range. I’ll engage it at a barely perceptible 3.41% blend. The threshold drops to 7.73 dB so it only acts on the quietest passages, paired with a gentle ratio of 0.185 and a soft knee to ensure the cutoff is smooth and natural. This tightens the decay without any audible gating artifacts. Commit: engage at 3.41% (drywet_fraction 0.0341), drop threshold_db to 7.73 (log_threshold 1.78), soften ratio_softplus to 0.185 (log_ratio -1.596), set log_knee to 0.292, and apply z_alpha_pre -8.735.

For gain and panning, the track sits too far back with an unbalanced stereo image; the left channel is sitting at -10.46 dB and the right at -3.1 dB, pushing the instrument off-center. I’ll raise the left channel to -7.0 dB and push the right channel up to +3.19 dB to bring the piano forward and recenter it, shifting the LR balance to -10.19 dB. I’ll blend the module to 58.56% to apply this adjustment subtly, preserving the original tracking intent while fixing the mix balance. Commit: raise left gain to -7.0 dB and push right to +3.19 dB (log_gain [-0.806, 0.367]), shift lr_balance_db to -10.19, and blend to 58.56% (drywet_fraction 0.5856).

The EQ and stereo imager modules are already aligned with the target tonal and spatial character, so no adjustments are needed there.

I need to roll off the high frequencies aggressively to tame the brightness and bring the overall level in line. I need to lower the threshold to -18.92 dB (cmp_th -18.918) and increase the ratio to 2.62 (cmp_ratio -2.372) to clamp down on the dynamics. The attack and release must be much faster to catch the transients tightly, so I will set the attack coefficient to 0.0179 (at -4.003) and release to 0.0002 (rt -8.326). I will drop the makeup gain to -0.49 dB (make_up -0.494) to compensate for the added gain reduction, and set the dry/wet to 0.4404. I will also engage the expander with a threshold of -45.07 dB (exp_th -45.068) and ratio of 1.42 (exp_ratio -3.782). For the reverb, the current fifty-percent mix and 665 ms mean decay are too short and dry, failing to blend the keys. I will increase the dry/wet to 0.6442 and extend the decay to a mean of 854.7 ms, with a minimum of 50.7 ms and maximum of 2000.0 ms. I will adjust the band decay and gain parameters to create a more complex, colored tail, targeting a mean absolute band gain of 0.5443 and applying the calculated log_decay and log_gain arrays. Finally, the stereo imager is currently boosting the sides by +2.0 dB at fifty percent mix, creating an unnaturally wide image.
